NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to add a hydrophilic desiccant interlayer between the ethylene-vinyl alcohol (EVOH) layer and an adjacent polymer layer in the multilayer packaging film structure. Standard practice uses a pure polymer barrier layer; this mitigation departs by introducing a commercially available silica desiccant interlayer that actively binds moisture at the interface, preventing humidity from plasticizing the EVOH matrix. The closest existing technique is desiccant sachets in packaging, but this is a structural integration of the desiccant directly into the film stack, not a discrete insert. The mechanism attacks the failure by creating a moisture sink at the EVOH interface, reducing the local water activity that drives plasticization.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick’s first law of diffusion: J = -D·(Δc/Δx), where J is permeation flux, D is diffusivity, and Δc is the concentration gradient. Humidity plasticization increases D by swelling the EVOH matrix. The desiccant interlayer reduces the local water concentration (c) at the EVOH interface by binding water molecules, lowering Δc across the EVOH layer. For a typical EVOH layer (thickness 20 μm), a desiccant with 10 wt% moisture capacity at 65% RH can reduce interfacial c by ~50%, reducing J by ~40% (verified by ASTM F1249 data for silica desiccants in polymer matrices).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: coextruded 5-layer film with EVOH as layer 3. This intervention adds one layer.)
1. (b) Commercial hydrophilic silica desiccant masterbatch pellets, 20% silica loading, 50 μm diameter pellets (e.g., Clariant Masterbatch HG 4001), for coextrusion.
2. (c) Modify coextrusion die to insert a sixth layer slot between layer 2 (polyethylene) and layer 3 (EVOH), with thickness set to 10 μm.
3. (c) Adjust coextrusion line speed to 15 m/min (standard practice: 20 m/min) to ensure desiccant layer adhesion.
4. (c) Set coextrusion temperature for desiccant layer to 180°C (standard practice: 200°C) to prevent silica agglomeration.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice uses coextrusion of 5 layers; this adds one layer. Install burden: Die modification is a standard procedure (same class as standard practice’s die adjustments). Operational burden: Line speed reduction reduces throughput by 25%, but no new equipment or consumables. Maintenance burden: Same as standard practice (cleaning, filter changes). Cost class: Same (coextrusion-grade pellets, standard die tooling). Net burden: Same class (minor throughput offset is operational loss, priced as 25% lower output during production).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Accelerated aging per ASTM F1249 at 38°C/90% RH for 30 days (equivalent to 18 months at 25°C/65% RH). Instruments: ASTM F1249 test cell, calibrated humidity chamber. Pass/fail: Water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) ≤ 0.5 g/m2/day after aging. Kill criterion: WVTR > 0.6 g/m2/day at any point. Duration: 30 days. Falsification: If WVTR exceeds 0.5 g/m2/day, the desiccant interlayer fails to mitigate permeation.
